title: Chapter 161: Scary Livestream
html:
The one-armed man landed hard on his backside, his remaining arm hanging uselessly at his side.

“One on one is much fairer.”

Iron hammer in hand, Chen Ge turned toward the twisted-faced man. A doctor’s coat hung from his frame, and signs of skin grafts distorted his features. Chen Ge needed no introduction. The moment he saw the man, he swung for his shoulder.

The Third Sick Hall was tonight’s true objective. Before entering, Chen Ge intended to neutralize as many dangers as possible. They had technically never met, and the twisted-faced man had not expected such merciless aggression from his supposed prey.

The assault frightened even genuine madmen. The twisted-faced man recoiled, spun, and fled down the corridor. His one-armed companion moved faster still. Years of relying on his legs had made his lower body exceptionally strong; a single roll brought him upright, and he sprinted away without looking back.

Neither attempted to fight. Their immediate retreat surprised Chen Ge, but he recovered quickly and pursued them with Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer.

Pounding footsteps shattered the night’s silence. The “victim” trapped in the psychiatric hospital now chased two “culprits” through its halls, wielding an enormous hammer. The pursuit was too fierce for anyone to exchange a word.

Chen Ge followed them from the third floor down to the first. Familiar with the building, the two patients darted into a secluded stairwell. He pursued them all the way to the fourth floor, but as they passed the third-floor corridor again, they split up.

“They’re splitting up?” He had not expected them to coordinate, but his choice was easy. “I already disabled the one-armed man’s only arm. The twisted-faced one is more dangerous. If I take him down, entering the Third Sick Hall will be much safer.”

The instant Chen Ge pursued the twisted-faced man, however, the one-armed man stopped and doubled back to block him. His companion seized the opening, raced to the fourth floor, and headed for the passage connecting the buildings.

“Every passage between the second and third halls has a security door. The second-floor lock rusted shut, and I never checked the third. Does the fourth-floor door still work?”

As the one-armed man charged, Chen Ge responded without hesitation: he swung at the man’s legs. Within seconds, he had shaken him off and resumed his sprint upstairs.

The twisted-faced man’s eyes twitched as he fled. Never before had he encountered prey this aggressive. He wrenched open the steel door between the buildings and escaped into the Third Sick Hall.

Chen Ge watched him vanish but did not follow. The corridor ahead resembled a monster’s throat, and every instinct warned him away as the stench grew thicker.

“The Third Sick Hall…” At the threshold, he examined the steel door. Someone had sawed through its lock. “If these people have a saw, being captured would end very badly.”

The chase had lasted more than ten minutes and left him winded. He marked the steel door with a line of salt, returned to the second sick hall, and dragged the incapacitated one-armed man into the laundry room.

All three prisoners reacted to his arrival. The young woman’s response was most violent; she hurled herself against the cage as if desperate to escape the room itself.

“What did you do to traumatize an ordinary woman until she lost her mind?” This was why Chen Ge felt no sympathy for either attacker. Both had participated in something monstrous.

As the one-armed man lay unconscious, Chen Ge noticed something odd. Not once had he cried out when the hammer struck his arm or legs.

“Can he not feel pain?” Chen Ge was not deranged enough to test the idea. He bound the man to a pipe in the room’s corner with strips of dirty cloth, retrieved the fallen wrist camera, and strapped it back on. “Now that I have the advantage, it’s time to enter the Third Sick Hall.”

A glance at the livestream shocked him: more than eighty thousand people were watching, and the number kept rising. The earlier action had apparently propelled his broadcast beyond those of many established hosts.

“My stream must be more exciting than Qin Guang’s. At this rate, I’ll steal some of his viewers.” He checked the chat, only to find the rapidly growing audience slipping out of control.

People hidden beneath filthy laundry, a one-armed attacker struck with a hammer, and a ten-minute chase through a psychiatric hospital—nothing like it had ever appeared on the platform. The livestream was on the verge of exploding in popularity.

Some viewers praised his dedication and attention to detail; others mocked the spectacle as exaggerated. A smaller, morally concerned group wanted to call the police after seeing people locked in cages. Their intense reactions surprised Chen Ge. Fortunately, he had never revealed the exact location, mentioning only a mysterious abandoned psychiatric hospital.

Eighty thousand viewers sounded enormous, but against the country’s population, it was a drop in the ocean. Even the few residents of Jiujiang among them might never have heard of the Jiujiang Third Psychological Convalescence Centre, abandoned for years.

Without an address, police intervention was unlikely. Even if viewers pieced together his location from the broadcast, midnight would probably have passed by then. Hiding the fearsome hammer behind his back, Chen Ge addressed the camera to calm everyone, steering the conversation toward excellent acting and a meticulously written script.

The deception was not easy. Other hosts feared having their fiction exposed and spent heavily on original scripts, actors, and carefully staged scares.

Chen Ge had the opposite problem. Everything was so real that even he was frightened, and the “surprises” kept coming—each worse than the last.
